rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes that rujz is recited with rā either vowelled u or i.
rows.anchor: râ’nın zammı veya kesri ile وَٱلرُّجْزَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rujz can mean filth or punishment; here it is also explained as idols and images.
rows.anchor: pislik ve azab mânasına geldiği gibi burada putlar, esnâm ve evsân demek olduğunu da beyan etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of menn is to avoid boasting by counting one's deeds, service, or kindness as great.
rows.anchor: “Menn” başa kakmak mânasına olarak “yaptığın işi, hizmeti, iyiliği çok sayarak başa kakma

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Menn can mean giving: do good solely for God, without seeking a larger return, worldly gain, or display.
rows.anchor: mahza[^1] Allah için iyilik et, başkasından bir ecir bekleme.” Bu mâna İbn Abbas’tan menkuldür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With either sense of menn, tastakthiru is circumstantial, meaning mustakthiran.
rows.anchor: Bu iki mânada تَسْتَكْثِرُ cümlesi hâldir, مُسْتَكْثِراً demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jussive reading as the response to prohibition would mean not reproaching a good deed so as to increase reward; it is absent from the ten readings, though a non-resultative sense remains possible.
rows.anchor: terettüb kasdedilmeyerek şu mâna da olabilir: Yaptığın hizmeti başa kakma

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to endure the hardships and harms of carrying out these duties purely for his Lord.
rows.anchor: bu vazifeleri yapmak için her ne kadar zahmetler çekecek, ezâlar görecek isen de mahza Rabbinin hükmü için artık sabreyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqur is a mouth-blown horn; the root can mean striking, picking, or sounding a horn, linked to air pressure and sound striking the ears.
rows.anchor: sûr gibi ağızla üflenerek çalınan boruya denir, nakr vurmak ve didiklemek mânalarına geldiği gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A horn blast conventionally commands a caravan or army to set out; here it signals the divinely commanded journey of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: borusu ötmek de emir ve kumandasının nüfûzundan kinaye olduğu cihetle nakr-i nâkūr, nefh-i sûr, âhiret seferi için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means when the trumpet is blown, and the intended blast is the first one; Elmalılı links it to the single blast in al-Naziat.
rows.anchor: Fâ ta‘lîliye olarak اذا نفخ في الصور demektir. Burada murad nefha-i ûlâ olduğu beyan olunuyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin substitutes for a genitive complement: yauma idh kana kadha, meaning that day when it is so.
rows.anchor: Tenvin, muzâf-ı ileyhden ivazdır. يوم اذ كان كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added statement that the day is not easy distinguishes difficulty that grows and never relents from hardship that eventually becomes manageable.
rows.anchor: zorluk iki türlüdür. Birisi evvelâ çok zor olmakla beraber gittikçe kolaylaşır, yenilebilir. Birisi de gittikçe zorlaşır, hiç kolaylaşmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahidan can be a circumstantial phrase for the Creator, uniquely creating without a partner, or for the created person, made solitary and unsupported.
rows.anchor: mahluk olan تَمْنُن’den de hâl olabilir. Yani Benimle bırak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of being created alone applies to every individual, as in the verse that people will come singly as first created.
rows.anchor: her ferd hakkında sahihtir. Ve bununla kıyametin de hilkat gibi bilhassa ferdî safhasına işaret buyurulmuş demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points to an individual phase of resurrection, just as creation began with each person alone.
rows.anchor: kıyametin de hilkat gibi bilhassa ferdî safhasına işaret buyurulmuş demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion of revelation is reported to have been al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi.
rows.anchor: Bunun sebeb-i nüzûlü Velîd b. Mugīre el-Mahzûmî olduğu rivayet olunuyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the occasion is specific, the warning applies generally according to the traits described.
rows.anchor: Sebeb-i nüzûlün has olması hüküm ve inzârın vasıflara nazaran umûmî olmasına mâni‘de değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the wording hints that al-Walid was a foundling or illegitimate claimant, as discussed in Surat Nun, and was called Wahid.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Nûn’da geçtiği vechile zenîm, da‘iyy olduğuna îmâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mamdud means extended or abundant wealth, including property and estates, or wealth continually increased by growth or trade.
rows.anchor: uzun uzadıya uzatılmış, yani çok mal, servet, arazi ve çiftlik gibi geniş yahut nemâ ile veya ticaret ile artırılmış uzatılmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe al-Walid as owning extensive assets between Mecca and Taif, an all-season fruit garden in Taif, and roughly a million coins.
rows.anchor: Velîd’in Mekke ile Tâif arasında türlü emvâli ve Tâif’te yaz kış meyveleri eksik olmayan bostanı ve milyon kadar nukūdu bulunduğuna dair rivayetler nakledilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhud is the plural of shahid: sons present with their father, free to attend gatherings and consulted for testimony, opinions, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: hazır hepsi yanında, göz önünde, çalışmak için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say al-Walid had ten or thirteen adult sons; seven are identified: Walid, Khalid, Umara, Hisham, As, Qays, and Abd Shams.
rows.anchor: Denilmiş ki Velîd b. Mugīre’nin hepsi ricâlden olmak üzere on veya on üç oğlu vardı, fakat mâlum olan yedidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Khalid, Hisham, and Walid embraced Islam.
rows.anchor: Denilmiş ki: Bunlardan Hâlid, Hişam, Velîd[^2] şeref-i İslâm ile müşerref olmuşlar

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf instead names Khalid, Hisham, and Umara as the three sons who embraced Islam.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf böyle أَسْلَمَ مِنـْهُمْ

rows.speaker: آلوسي
rows.claim: Alusi reports disagreement over whether Umara was killed at Badr or in Abyssinia by the Negus, but says both accounts agree he died an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Umâre’nin Bedir’de veya Habeşte Necâşî tarafından katledildiği ihtilâflıdır, iki rivayet de kâfiren katlinde müttefiktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects al-Thalabi's report from Muqatil that Umara converted; Ibn Hajar calls it an error, also repeated in al-Kashshaf and by its followers.
rows.anchor: İslâmına dair Sa‘lebî’nin Mukātil’den rivayeti sahih olmaz, İbn Hacer onun galat olduğunu tansis etmiştir. Bu galat sâhib-i Keşşâf’ta da vâki‘olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi notes with surprise that Walid ibn Walid was omitted despite hadith scholars unanimously affirming his conversion.
rows.anchor: Taaccüb olunur ki Velîd b. Velîd’i İslâm ile müşerref olanlar meyânında zikretmemişler, hâlbuki muhaddisîn baştan âhire onun islâmında müttefiktirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes that Walid ibn Walid later converted, Umara's conversion is disputed, and the remaining sons beyond four are unknown.
rows.anchor: Velîd b. Velîd’in de sonradan islâmında ihtilâf görülmüyor fakat Umâre ihtilâflı, dörtten mâ‘adâsı ise gayr-i mâlum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond wealth and sons, God prepared many means for al-Walid and granted him standing, grandeur, and good fortune.
rows.anchor: mal ve oğullardan başka, birçok esbâb ihzar ederek câh ve haşmet ü ikbal de verdim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid was counted among Quraysh's leading notables and was known as Wahid and Rayhanat Quraysh.
rows.anchor: Velîd Kureyş içinde vücûhtan, sanâdîdden sayılırdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid is reported to have said that if Muhammad were truthful, Paradise must have been created for him.
rows.anchor: Muhammed sâdık ise cennet benim için yaratılmış demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla is a particle of rejection, denying a statement, claim, hope, or request; here it cuts off al-Walid's expectation of more.
rows.anchor: Bir sözü, bir davayı veya ümit ve talebi reddeder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid stubbornly opposed either the proofs of the benefactor's oneness or the Quran's verses; this was ingratitude for the blessings.
rows.anchor: o nimetleri veren mün‘imin vahdâniyeti delillerine veya Kur’an âyetlerine karşı inada kalkıştı, bu ise küfrân-ı nimettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ingratitude for blessings leads to their withdrawal, not their increase.
rows.anchor: Nimete küfran ise onun [5455] artmasına değil, kesilmesine sebeptir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saud means a steep uphill climb, used here for a harsh, upright punishment.
rows.anchor: sa‘ûda: sarp yokuşa, dikine azâba sardıracağım

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith transmitted by Tirmidhi, Hakim, and others describes Saud as a mountain of fire climbed for seventy years before the climber falls inside.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm buyurmuştur ki: “Sa‘ûd ateşten bir dağdır

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report from the Prophet describes a hellish ascent where hands and feet melt when placed on it and return when lifted.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’den: “Cehennemde bir akabeye çıkması teklif olunur ki ona elini koydukça erir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that after the verse was revealed, al-Walid's wealth dwindled day by day until it was gone.
rows.anchor: rivayet olunuyor ki âyetin nüzûlünden sonra Velîd’in malı günden güne eksilmiş, nihâyet helâk olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains the threat's cause or his obstinacy: al-Walid thought and made a mental estimate, measuring and guessing.
rows.anchor: ve bir takdir yaptı zihninde ölçtü biçti, bir tahmin yaptı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutila and qatalahu Allah are curses, but can also express admiration; here the phrase mocks those praising al-Walid's calculation by echoing their praise contemptuously.
rows.anchor: burada onun düşüncesini beğenenlerin bu yoldaki senâlarını hikâye ile tahkir içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the curse intensifies the contempt and signals a change in the successive estimates.
rows.anchor: Bu tekrar, hem tahkīri tekid

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After calculating, he looked around at those nearby.
rows.anchor: Sonra baktı etrafındakilere bir bakındı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abasa means he frowned; basara means he grimaced and scowled.
rows.anchor: kaşını çattı {وَبَسَرَ} ve ekşidi, surat astı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basr can mean acting prematurely or rashly; unripe dates are called busur, and al-Raghib takes this as the sense here.
rows.anchor: Râgıb burada bu mânadan olduğunu söyler.[^14]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned from the truth, turned his back on faith toward unbelief, and arrogantly refused to acknowledge the truth.
rows.anchor: anlamış olduğu haktan yüz çevirdi, imana arkasını, küfre yüzünü döndürdü ve Allah’tan korkmayıp gurur ile büyüklük tasladı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the phrase as inherited magic, supposedly taught and passed down from one practitioner to another.
rows.anchor: yani öteden beri tâlim ve rivayet olunagelen ehlinden ehline öğrenilegeldiği söylenen bir sihir demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, yu'thar can mean magic preferred or admired above other magic, with a dazzling, captivating appeal.
rows.anchor: îsâr olunacak, sâir sihirlere tercih edilecek, beğenilecek bir sihir demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid settles on calling the Quran human speech, thereby denying the prophethood and the Quran's status as God's speech.
rows.anchor: Kararı bastı, risâleti ve Kur’ân’ın Allah kelâmı olmasını inkâr ediverdi

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: In the reported account, al-Walid first praised the Quran's sweetness, beauty, fruitfulness, and incomparable height, but later called it transmitted magic and human speech.
rows.anchor: Velîd b. Mugīre Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’nin yanına gelmiş, Kur’an dinlemiş, bir teessür duymuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Quraysh accused al-Walid of straying; Abu Jahl persuaded him to make a public denunciation despite al-Walid's wealth and expertise in poetry.
rows.anchor: bunu işiten Ebû Cehil “ben size onun hakkından gelirim” deyip

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Under pressure, al-Walid argued that Muhammad was not insane, a soothsayer, a poet, or a liar, yet produced the verdict of magic and human speech to satisfy the assembly.
rows.anchor: hiç kimseyi boğarken gördünüz mü? Kâhin diyorsunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account ends with the assembly applauding al-Walid's denunciation and dispersing.
rows.anchor: Bunun üzerine hoşlarına gitmiş, meclislerinde bir alkıştır kopmuş, onun sözünü alkışlayarak dağılmışlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some treat the incident as the occasion for the beginnings of al-Muzzammil and al-Muddaththir; Elmalılı says it concerns these verses, since the recited passages were from the Ha-Mims.
rows.anchor: Velîd’in dinlediği âyetler حٰمٓ’lerden olduğuna dair vâki‘olan rivayetlerden de anlaşıldığına göre bu, bu sûrenin başının değil, bu âyetlerinin sebeb-i nüzûlü olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse explicates the earlier threat of Saud and is an inclusive substitute for it.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet سَأُرْهِقُهُۥ صَعُودًا’den bedel-i iştimâldir ve onun mazmûnunu îzahtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call Saqar non-Arabic; Elmalılı prefers deriving it from sakr, the sun's scorching heat, giving it the sense of burning.
rows.anchor: Güneş’in yüzü çalıp kavurması mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means that Saqar is beyond what ordinary understanding can fully comprehend.
rows.anchor: o öyle bir sekar ki onun mâhiyetini dirayetle bilemezsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar consumes every particle of whatever it catches, yet does not release its victim; the victim is recreated and the punishment continues.
rows.anchor: bir kere çattığı bir şeyi hiçbir zerresi kalmayacak vechile helâk eder, tüketir, sonra da yakasını yine bırakmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar can mean human beings or the outer surfaces of skin, especially human skin; humans are called bashar for this visible skin.
rows.anchor: derinin bâhusus insan derisinin dış yüzleri mânasına da olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawwaha is an intensive form of lawh, whose senses include thirst, solar heat, scorching or darkening a face, appearing, flashing, or seeing.
rows.anchor: mübalağa sîgasıdır. “Levh” susamak veya Güneş’in harâreti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can picture Saqar as insatiably thirsty, constantly scorching and darkening faces, or continually watching for and attacking people; Elmalılı suggests an unquenchable thirst that burns humans.
rows.anchor: Kanmak bilmez bir susuz, mütemâdiyen beşer-sûz

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains lawwaha as continuously scorching human faces and making them dark.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: Mütemâdiyen beşereler kavuran, yüzler karartan mânası mervîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counted noun or qualifier after nineteen is omitted; the next verse shows that the referent is the guardians of Hell.
rows.anchor: Bu on dokuzun ne olduğunu anlatan mümeyyizi zikrolunmuyor. Ancak bundan sonraki âyetten o cehennemin korucuları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attempts to explain the number through human spiritual or moral faculties miss the point: it is an unknowable divine report and a test of faith, whose interpretation is left to God.
rows.anchor: doğrusu bunun dirayetle bilinecek bir ilim işi değil, mutlak bir iman işi olmak üzere imtihan için olduğu ikinci âyette bilhassa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has powers and forces humans cannot yet understand, whose reality He alone knows; believers should accept the revealed report unconditionally.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın şimdi sizin tamamen bilip anlayamayacağınız ve ileride tezahür edecek öyle kuvvet ve kudretleri vardır ki onların hakikatini ancak kendisi bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashab al-nar means the fire's keepers or guardians, not its eternal inhabitants; these are the angelic keepers of Hell, led by Malik.
rows.anchor: ebediyen o ateş içinde kalıp yanacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers are the stern angels described in al-Tahrim, called the keepers of Hell and led by Malik.
rows.anchor: ve reisleri Mâlik olan zebâni meleklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their number means the nineteen just mentioned.
rows.anchor: yani adetlerinden murad da zikrolunan تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ adedi olduğu vâzıhtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the number nineteen, while leaving unclear whether it counts individuals or kinds, is a trial for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: sayılarının on dokuz yapılması veya şahısları mı nevileri mi ne olduğu tâyin edilmeyerek sade on dokuz adediyle muammâ hâlinde ifade ve ihbar olunması mücerred kâfirlere bir mihnet ve imtihan içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know scripture and the limits of present human judgment have doubts dispelled, while receptive believers gain faith and are guided toward success and salvation.
rows.anchor: kitap ve peygamberin ne demek olduğunu ve istikbal işinin bugünkü kıyaslarla bilinemeyeceğini bilenlerin işkillerini kesecek ve iman kābiliyeti olanların imanlarını artırarak muvaffakiyet ve halâslarına bâ‘is olacak

words: لِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ وَٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People without faith or with diseased hearts may treat the report as a puzzling riddle and use it to ridicule and deny revelation.
rows.anchor: alay ve inkâra sapmalarına sebep olabilirse de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says Abu Jahl mocked the nineteen guardians and challenged Quraysh's strong men; Abu al-Ashadd claimed he could defeat seventeen while others handled two, after which the verse identified them as angels.
rows.anchor: Ebû Cehil Kureyş’e şöyle demişti: “Analarınız ağlasın, [^7] Ebû Kebşe’nin oğlunu işitiyorum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says the clarification that the keepers were angels was revealed in response to the boast that men could overpower them.
rows.anchor: nâzil oldu. “Onlar sizin tâkat getireceğiniz adamlar değil, melâikedir” diye haber verildi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account also says verses from Surat al-Qiyama were revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: Ve Ebû Cehil hakkında da Sûre-i Kıyâme’deki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh report from Jabir that Jews asked companions whether their Prophet knew the keepers' number; the Prophet indicated ten and then nine with his fingers.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî ve İbn Merdûye’nin Hazret-i Câbir’den bir rivayetlerine göre: Yahudîlerden bazı kimseler Peygamber’in ashabından bazılarına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer a Medinan date because Jews lived in Medina, but Elmalılı considers the inference weak: companions could visit Medina or Jews could visit Mecca, and the story may be explanatory rather than an occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: ashabdan bazılarının Medine’ye veya Yahudîlerden bazılarının Mekke’ye gitmiş olmaları melhuz bulunduğundan bu istidlâlin zayıf olduğu derkârdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Junud is the plural of jund, meaning soldiers, helpers, troops, or armies; it is associated with military strength and harshness and derives from jund, rocky hard terrain.
rows.anchor: cem‘idir ki asker ve bir adamın a‘vân u ensârı, alay ve ordu mânalarına gelir

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows His forces; the incomprehensible number is meant to establish unconditional belief in this truth.
rows.anchor: İşte o muammânın asıl sırrı ve fâidesi bu hakikate mutlak bir imanı temin etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may refer either to Saqar or to these verses; in either case it is a reminder and benefit for humanity.
rows.anchor: ancak beşer için, beşerin menfaati için bir öğüt, bir muhtıradır
